And we know that all things work together for good to
them that love God, to them who are the called according
to his purpose –Romans 8:28.

“I’ve been thinking that we could take a trip next week with school being off.” Arthur said, hanging his hat on the hook in the utility room and turning to his wife. “What do you think about such an idea?”

Myrtle, who had been busy preparing supper in the kitchen, looked up with a smile. “That would be great, I have been having similar thoughts. I’m sure the children would enjoy a vacation as well.”

“Why don’t we plan to visit the congregation at Bethel Fellowship next Sunday then?” Arthur continued. “Would that suit you?”

“Yes, I think so,” Myrtle answered. “It seems like it has been a little while since we went visiting to another congregation. When were you thinking of leaving?”

“I haven’t made definite plans yet,” Arthur replied, “but I was thinking of leaving Thursday and coming home on Monday.”

“That sounds fine to me,” Myrtle answered.

“Alright,” Arthur said. “I’ll plan to send a letter to Brother Oscar Peight to let them know we’re coming.”

The next Thursday found the Coblentz family heading for Pennsylvania.

Many miles passed uneventfully as the family traveled north. They were getting closer to their destination when suddenly Arthur got sick. He pulled their van off the road so he could empty his stomach’s contents. Patiently the family waited, wondering what they should do next.

“Do you think we should go on?” Myrtle inquired. It would be another hour before they reached Brother Oscar’s place.

“I don’t see how I can go on,” Arthur responded weakly. “I feel really dizzy now. Maybe you should take over driving now,” he said to Myrtle.

Soon the drivers had switched places. It was with disappointed hearts that the family turned around and headed back home. It was difficult for the whole family, especially the children. They had looked forward to this trip all week long, and now their plans were spoiled.

Upon arriving home, Myrtle stopped at the mailbox to get their mail. She handed the mail to Arthur, then drove in their lane.

“Why…. What’s this?” Arthur sputtered, spying a familiar envelope. He ripped open the envelope and could not believe what he saw. “The letter I sent to Brother Oscar Peight!” Why ever had it been returned? His heart sank as he turned over the envelope. “Of all things, I forgot to put a stamp on the envelope!” he exclaimed. “How silly was that!”

That evening at the supper table, the family once more discussed how foolish it seemed to have forgotten to stick a stamp in the corner of that envelope. “But yet,” Arthur marveled, “God had all this planned. If that letter would have reached Brother Oscars, they would have been preparing for us. But this way, they did not even know we were coming to visit.”

“All things do work together for good to them that love God,” Myrtle replied.

우리는 하나님을 사랑하는 사람들, 곧 그분의 뜻에 따라 부르심을 받은 사람들에게는 모든 일이 합력하여 선을 이룬다는 것을 압니다.
–로마서 8:28.

“학교가 쉬니까 다음 주에 여행을 다녀오면 어떨까 생각하고 있었어요.” 아서는 다용도실의 고리에 모자를 걸고 아내를 돌아보며 말했다. “그런 생각에 대해 어떻게 생각해요?”

부엌에서 저녁 식사를 준비하느라 바쁘던 머틀은 웃으며 고개를 들었다. “정말 좋겠어요. 저도 비슷한 생각을 하고 있었거든요. 아이들도 휴가를 즐길 거라고 확신해요.”

“그럼 다음 주 일요일에 베델 펠로십의 회중을 방문하는 것으로 계획해 보면 어떨까요?” 아서가 말을 이었다. “괜찮겠어요?”

“네, 좋을 것 같아요.” 머틀이 대답했다. “다른 회중을 방문하러 간 지 좀 된 것 같네요. 언제 떠날 생각이에요?”

“아직 확실히 정한 건 없어요.” 아서가 대답했다. “하지만 목요일에 떠나서 월요일에 돌아오면 어떨까 생각했어요.”

“저는 좋아요.” 머틀이 대답했다.

“좋아요.” 아서가 말했다. “오스카 페이트 형제에게 편지를 보내서 우리가 간다는 걸 알리도록 할게요.”

그다음 목요일, 코블렌츠 가족은 펜실베이니아로 향했다.

가족이 북쪽으로 여행하는 동안 여러 마일을 별일 없이 지나갔다. 목적지에 가까워졌을 때 갑자기 아서가 몸이 아파졌다. 그는 속을 비우려고 밴을 도로 옆에 세웠다. 가족은 다음에 어떻게 해야 할지 고민하며 참을성 있게 기다렸다.

“계속 가야 할까요?” 머틀이 물었다. 오스카 형제의 집까지는 한 시간 더 가야 했다.

“계속 갈 수 있을 것 같지 않아요.” 아서는 힘없이 대답했다. “지금은 정말 어지러워요. 이제 당신이 운전대를 잡는 게 좋겠어요.” 그는 머틀에게 말했다.

이내 운전자가 바뀌었다. 실망한 마음으로 가족은 차를 돌려 집으로 향했다. 가족 모두에게 힘든 일이었지만, 특히 아이들에게 그랬다. 아이들은 한 주 내내 이 여행을 손꼽아 기다렸는데, 이제 계획이 엉망이 되어 버렸다.

집에 도착한 머틀은 우편함에 들러 우편물을 꺼냈다. 우편물을 아서에게 건네고는 진입로를 따라 차를 몰았다.

“아니…. 이게 뭐지?” 아서는 익숙한 봉투를 발견하고는 당황해서 말을 더듬었다. 봉투를 뜯은 그는 눈앞에 보이는 것을 믿을 수 없었다. “오스카 페이트 형제에게 보낸 편지잖아!” 도대체 왜 반송된 걸까? 봉투를 뒤집어 보자 그의 마음이 가라앉았다. “이럴 수가, 봉투에 우표 붙이는 걸 깜빡했어!” 그가 외쳤다. “정말 어리석었네!”

그날 저녁 식탁에서 가족은 그 봉투 모퉁이에 우표 붙이는 걸 잊어버린 일이 얼마나 어리석게 보였는지 다시 이야기했다. “그런데도 말이야.” 아서는 놀라워하며 말했다. “하나님께서는 이 모든 일을 계획해 두셨던 거야. 그 편지가 오스카 형제 가족에게 도착했다면, 그들은 우리를 맞을 준비를 하고 있었겠지. 하지만 이렇게 되어서 그들은 우리가 방문하러 간다는 것도 전혀 몰랐어.”

“하나님을 사랑하는 사람들에게는 모든 일이 합력하여 선을 이루지요.” 머틀이 대답했다.

While the earth remaineth, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease –Genesis 8:22. Greetings to one and all. As I am writing this, it is the beginning of May and yet in our area it still seems as though spring has not yet quite arrived. There are glimmers of hope that summer surely will come—some of the trees are pushing their leaves and select early flowers have pushed their blossoms up to wave bravely in the cool, damp breezes. Yet, overall, the weather seems to feel much more like the month of March.

This coming week has the promise of warm, dry weather, which should make many area farmers and homeowners happy. We are anticipating a great bevy of activity as gardens and fields are tilled and seeded with this year’s crops. To those who read the Holy Scriptures and who believe the written Word of God, these normal day-to-day activities should be a reminder of God’s promises in the same way as each new sighting of a rainbow.

And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet. For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places –Matthew 24:6-7.

And there shall be … pestilences … in divers places

In February or March of 2020, COVID-19 was declared a pandemic (a disease that spreads rapidly and affects a large percentage of the population). Now, over two years later, health officials and government leaders are somewhat reticent to publicly declare that the crisis has passed.

Some parts of the world have lifted all regulations regarding COVID-19 such as Denmark and England, while others such as New Zealand are still quite rigid with their ongoing rules and guidelines. And quite recently Chinese officials again locked down certain areas of their country in their efforts to quash a recent outbreak of new infections.

Many, if not most, individuals are tired of it all, ready for it to be over, and anxious to get back to life as normal. Many have lost loved ones. Many have endured financial setbacks and economic loss. Recent data from the World Health Organization (WHO) provides the approximate deaths (both direct and indirect) from COVID-19 to be around 15 million for the first two years of the pandemic.

While recent data from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimates that the median global GDP dropped by 3.9% from 2019 to 2020, making it the worst economic downturn since the Great Depression, creating a global recession that is the deepest since the end of World War 2.

Recently, a brother mentioned to me that “the world is in a mess” and that he has heard realtors, auctioneers, and financial advisors say that the world of finance is in unprecedented waters and that no one knows where, when, or how it will all end.

However, we should not be surprised by this major worldwide struggle. The Scriptures foretell of famine and hunger, pestilence and death, plagues of all varieties, and the list goes on of things that will come upon the earth just prior to the end of time: …for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet –Matthew 24:6.

And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars

In recent years there have been numerous wars and rumors of wars. However, since February 24, 2022 when Russia launched its current full-scale invasion of Ukraine, there have been increased worries voiced by media and politicians about how this seems different. With the many sanctions enacted by the EU and the west, there have been ripple effects causing negative outcomes for many of the world’s economies, with sky-rocketing prices for many items and services being the outcome. Sure, there were high prices before this recent outbreak of war which was a result of the various supply chain problems that were caused by COVID-19 and its ripple effects. But since the sanctions were enacted against Russia the gas and oil prices have risen noticeably which in turn has caused the cost of most goods and services to follow suit.

What about all the what if ’s…? If this happens then “there will be a nuclear war.” If this happens then “it will cause World War 3 to begin.” “The Democrats are taking the U.S. to war with Russia.” These and many more comments are being made in our world today. To me it seems that when countries and individuals …trust in chariots, and some in horses: Psalm 20:7a, then their outcome will be that They are brought down and [are] fallen… –Psalm 20:8a. But if …we will remember the name of the LORD our God –Psalm 20:7b, then …we are risen, and [will] stand upright –Psalm 20:8b.

From my perspective it seems that many in the world have allowed fear to take root in their hearts during the whole COVID-19 ordeal. Now whenever some new “scary” development surfaces in this current Russia/Ukraine conflict and the many issues connected to it, again fear seems to be the prevailing motivator. This gives us a glimpse of what things will be like some day soon when: Men’s hearts [are] failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken –Luke 21:26. Because …those men which have not the seal of God in their foreheads … should be tormented five months … and shall desire to die, and death shall flee from them –Revelation 9:4-6. Also, there will come a day when …the kings of the earth, and the great men, and the rich men, and the chief captains, and the mighty men, and every bondman, and every free man, [will hide] themselves in the dens and in the rocks of the mountains; And [will say] to the mountains and rocks, Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb: For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand? –Revelation 6:15-17.

The worth of a soul

Then said Jesus unto his disciples, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me. For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it. For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul? –Matthew 16:24-26.

Recently, this verse came to my mind as I was thinking of a number of situations in our world today—both close to home and abroad.

First, that which is abroad…

I am one of those who enjoys relaxing on the porch of a house, which is located along a major highway, and watching the traffic. I also find it interesting to sit in an airport or bus terminal and observe the masses of people passing by. Many times, I have paused to consider that each one has a soul that will spend all of eternity somewhere! Alive! As I’ve pondered these thoughts, some further thoughts also come. “How many of these people have a personal awareness of eternity?” “Of life after death?” “Or of a God who is alive, sovereign, and holy who will some day require an accounting for all things done in this earthly body?”

How many of us bear a burden for the lost souls around us? I think of the testimony of a vehicle mechanic who told me how he prays and seeks the Lord’s leading about how he can speak into the lives of those who come to his shop. And of his further testimony regarding the various ways that God has led and folks have been pointed to a Living God and a life after death.

For many of us, for me in particular, it takes an effort to remember to stop and smell the roses or to pause and reflect on the beauty of a sunrise. Then it takes a further step to remember the Creator behind these earthly beauties. How much more can we become lulled into the sameness of our everyday lives and tend to forget that each soul we meet will someday stand before God? What if we were the one who God wanted to say a word for Him out of a life that was living for Him to bring His awareness to one who knows not the One, Living, and True God?

Now for that which is close…

This can take on many different situations. It can be those in our family. It can be our neighbors. It can be our more distant relatives. It can be our work associates. Finally, it can be anyone who we interact with in our daily lives.

Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me. Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee? or thirsty, and gave thee drink? When saw we thee a stranger, and took thee in? or naked, and clothed thee? Or when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came unto thee? And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me –Matthew 25:34-40.

One specific thing that I wish to focus on is this growing problem of broken relationships and emotional/mental struggles within the plain communities. I do not wish to pass judgment on anyone, nor do I wish to make anyone feel bad. In fact, one of my strongest concerns regarding these issues is that the church would do everything that it can to take away the stigma or negativity of these struggles. How did Christ relate to those who were in these types of situations? We could get hung up on the details of how Jesus responded. Let’s not allow details to hinder us from “being Christ” to these struggling individuals in our midst.

To bring perspective to how we approach and interact with someone who is struggling, we can ask ourselves several questions that will help. First a question for myself: “How would I appreciate someone responding to me if I was in that specific situation?” Second a question for the other person: “What can I do that would be a help or an encouragement to you as you are going through this difficult experience?”

Too many times, the church doesn’t have time for those who are struggling in their midst, since it is their lot in life and we are too busy to be bothered. Other times, the church doesn’t know how to respond or what to say so they decide it is better to “leave sleeping dogs lie” or that it would be best to not “open that can of worms”.

God designed us in such a way that we need our brothers and sisters. Just consider all the “one-anothering” passages in the Scriptures. Then consider how we can “be Christ” to the struggling among us. Just remember that there may come a time when “the shoe is on the other foot”, so to speak. In other words, someday we may find ourselves in a similar situation wishing that our brothers and sisters would rally around us with love and encouragement in a real way that “helps”.

Resources

It has been a while since we have reminded our readers that we have select resources on a variety of topics to assist churches and individuals as they seek a practical way forward that is pleasing to God. One resource, that is specific on the topic of how to help those in our midst, is an 8 CD set we put together titled “People Helping in the Local Church”. We have received feedback from many individuals and church leaders who have said that they found the information shared in this set to be very helpful in their efforts to understand how to “help” challenging situations in their midst.

Our resources are available free of charge to addresses located within the U.S. However, we are funded solely on the free-will offerings of God’s people, so your donation would be helpful to continue our work. If you wish to receive one or more of these CD sets, please contact our ministry using the contact information listed inside the front cover of this magazine.

Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, To the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen. – Jude 1:24-25.

땅이 있는 동안에는 심는 때와 거두는 때와 추위와 더위와 여름과 겨울과 낮과 밤이 그치지 아니하리라 –창세기 8:22. 여러분 모두에게 문안드립니다. 이 글을 쓰는 지금은 5월 초인데도, 우리 지역에는 아직 봄이 완전히 찾아오지 않은 듯합니다. 여름은 반드시 오리라는 희망의 조짐이 보입니다. 나무 몇 그루는 잎을 내고 있고, 일찍 피는 몇몇 꽃은 차고 축축한 바람 속에서도 용감하게 흔들리며 꽃봉오리를 밀어 올렸습니다. 하지만 전반적으로 날씨는 3월과 훨씬 더 비슷하게 느껴집니다.

이번 주에는 따뜻하고 건조한 날씨가 예보되어 있어, 이 지역의 많은 농부와 집주인들이 반길 것입니다. 밭과 정원을 갈고 올해 작물을 파종하면서 분주한 활동이 펼쳐질 것으로 기대하고 있습니다. 성경을 읽고 기록된 하나님의 말씀을 믿는 사람들에게, 이러한 평범한 일상은 새롭게 무지개를 볼 때마다 그러하듯 하나님의 약속을 상기시켜 주어야 합니다.

또 너희가 전쟁과 전쟁의 소문을 듣겠으나, 너희는 삼가 두려워하지 말라. 이런 일이 반드시 일어나야 하되 아직 끝은 아니니라. 민족이 민족을, 나라가 나라를 대적하여 일어나겠고, 곳곳에 기근과 전염병과 지진이 있으리라 –마태복음 24:6-7.

곳곳에 … 전염병이 있으리라

2020년 2월이나 3월에 코로나19는 팬데믹(빠르게 확산되어 인구의 상당한 비율에 영향을 미치는 질병)으로 선포되었습니다. 그로부터 2년이 넘게 지난 지금도 보건 당국자들과 정부 지도자들은 위기가 지나갔다고 공식적으로 선언하는 데 다소 주저하고 있습니다.

덴마크와 잉글랜드처럼 세계 일부 지역은 코로나19 관련 규제를 모두 해제했지만, 뉴질랜드와 같은 곳은 여전히 진행 중인 규칙과 지침을 상당히 엄격하게 시행하고 있습니다. 그리고 아주 최근에는 중국 당국자들이 새로운 감염이 다시 발생하자 이를 억제하기 위해 자국의 일부 지역을 또 봉쇄했습니다.

많은 사람들, 어쩌면 대부분의 사람들은 이 모든 일에 지쳐서 끝나기를 바라고, 일상적인 삶으로 돌아가기를 간절히 원합니다. 사랑하는 이를 잃은 사람도 많습니다. 재정적 어려움과 경제적 손실을 겪은 사람도 많습니다. 세계보건기구(WHO)의 최근 자료에 따르면 팬데믹 첫 2년 동안 코로나19로 인한 사망자 수는 직접 사망과 간접 사망을 합해 약 1,500만 명입니다.

한편 국제통화기금(IMF)의 최근 자료는 2019년부터 2020년까지 세계 중위 GDP가 3.9% 하락한 것으로 추정합니다. 이는 대공황 이후 최악의 경기 침체였으며, 제2차 세계대전이 끝난 이후 가장 심각한 세계적 경기 후퇴를 초래했습니다.

최근 한 형제가 제게 “세상이 엉망”이라고 말했습니다. 그는 부동산 중개인, 경매인, 재정 상담가들이 금융계가 전례 없는 상황에 놓여 있으며, 이 모든 일이 어디서, 언제, 어떻게 끝날지 아무도 모른다고 말하는 것을 들었다고 했습니다.

그러나 우리는 이처럼 전 세계적인 큰 어려움에 놀라서는 안 됩니다. 성경은 기근과 굶주림, 전염병과 죽음, 온갖 종류의 재앙을 예언하며, 세상 끝이 오기 직전에 땅에 닥칠 일들의 목록은 계속 이어집니다. …이런 일이 반드시 일어나야 하되 아직 끝은 아니니라 –마태복음 24:6.

또 너희가 전쟁과 전쟁의 소문을 들으리라

최근 몇 년 동안 수많은 전쟁과 전쟁의 소문이 있었습니다. 그러나 2022년 2월 24일 러시아가 우크라이나에 대한 현재의 전면 침공을 시작한 뒤로, 언론과 정치인들은 이 상황이 어떻게 다른지에 관해 더욱 큰 우려를 표명해 왔습니다. 유럽연합과 서방 국가들이 여러 제재를 시행하면서 세계 여러 경제에 부정적인 결과를 가져오는 파급 효과가 발생했고, 그 결과 많은 물품과 서비스의 가격이 치솟았습니다. 물론 이번 전쟁 발발 전에도 높은 물가가 있었습니다. 코로나19와 그 파급 효과로 생긴 여러 공급망 문제가 그 원인이었습니다. 그러나 러시아에 대한 제재가 시행된 뒤 가스와 석유 가격이 눈에 띄게 올랐고, 그에 따라 대부분의 상품과 서비스 비용도 뒤따라 상승했습니다.

그렇다면 온갖 ‘만약’은 어떻습니까…? 이것이 일어나면 “핵전쟁이 일어날 것이다.” 이것이 일어나면 “제3차 세계대전이 시작될 것이다.” “민주당이 미국을 러시아와의 전쟁으로 끌고 가고 있다.” 오늘날 세상에는 이런 말과 그 밖의 많은 말들이 오가고 있습니다. 제게는 나라들과 사람들이 …병거를 의지하고 어떤 이들은 말을 의지하나 –시편 20:7a, 그들의 결과는 그들은 엎드러지고 넘어지리로다… –시편 20:8a. 그러나 …우리는 우리 하나님 여호와의 이름을 기억하리로다 –시편 20:7b, 그렇게 한다면 그때 …우리는 일어나 바로 서리로다 –시편 20:8b.

제가 보기에는 많은 사람이 코로나19 사태 내내 두려움이 마음에 뿌리내리도록 내버려 둔 것 같습니다. 이제 러시아와 우크라이나의 현재 갈등과 그에 얽힌 여러 문제에서 새롭고 ‘무서운’ 전개가 하나라도 나타나면, 다시 두려움이 사람들을 움직이는 주된 동기가 되는 듯합니다. 이는 머지않은 어느 날 상황이 어떠할지 엿보게 합니다. 사람들이 세상에 임할 일들을 생각하고 무서워하므로 기절하리니, 이는 하늘의 권능들이 흔들리겠음이라 –누가복음 21:26. 이는 …하나님의 인이 그들의 이마에 없는 사람들 …이 다섯 달 동안 괴롭힘을 당하고 …죽기를 구하여도 죽음이 그들을 피하리라 –요한계시록 9:4-6. 또 어느 날에는 …땅의 왕들과 위대한 자들과 부자들과 천부장들과 용사들과 모든 종과 자유인이 굴과 산들의 바위 틈에 숨고, 산들과 바위들에게 이르되 우리 위에 무너져 보좌에 앉으신 이의 얼굴과 어린양의 진노에서 우리를 가리라. 그들의 진노의 큰 날이 이르렀으니 누가 능히 서리요 하리라 –요한계시록 6:15-17.

영혼의 가치

이에 예수께서 제자들에게 이르시되 누구든지 나를 따라오려거든 자기를 부인하고 자기 십자가를 지고 나를 따를 것이니라. 누구든지 자기 생명을 구원하고자 하면 잃을 것이요, 누구든지 나를 위하여 자기 생명을 잃으면 찾으리라. 사람이 온 세상을 얻고도 자기 영혼을 잃으면 무엇이 유익하리요? 사람이 자기 영혼과 바꾸어 무엇을 주겠느냐? –마태복음 16:24-26.

최근 우리 세상에서 가까운 곳과 먼 곳에서 벌어지는 여러 상황을 생각하다가 이 구절이 떠올랐습니다.

먼저, 먼 곳의 일입니다…

저는 큰 도로변에 있는 집의 현관에 앉아 쉬면서 오가는 차들을 구경하는 것을 좋아합니다. 공항이나 버스 터미널에 앉아 지나가는 수많은 사람을 바라보는 것도 흥미롭게 여깁니다. 저는 여러 번 잠시 멈추어 그들 각자에게 영혼이 있고, 그 영혼이 영원 내내 어딘가에서 살게 된다는 사실을 생각했습니다! 살아 있는 영혼입니다! 이런 생각을 곱씹다 보면 몇 가지 생각이 더 떠오릅니다. “이 사람들 가운데 얼마나 많은 이들이 영원을 개인적으로 인식하고 있을까?” “죽음 이후의 삶을 알고 있을까?” “혹은 살아 계시고 주권자이시며 거룩하신 하나님, 언젠가 이 땅의 몸으로 행한 모든 일에 대해 결산을 요구하실 하나님을 알고 있을까?”

우리 주변의 잃어버린 영혼들을 위해 우리 중 얼마나 많은 이들이 부담을 품고 있습니까? 한 자동차 정비공의 간증이 생각납니다. 그는 자신의 정비소에 오는 사람들의 삶에 어떤 말을 전할 수 있을지 주님의 인도하심을 구하며 기도한다고 제게 말했습니다. 또한 하나님께서 여러 방식으로 인도하셔서 사람들이 살아 계신 하나님과 죽음 이후의 삶을 가리키게 된 일들에 대해서도 간증했습니다.

많은 사람에게, 특히 저에게는, 잠시 멈추어 장미 향기를 맡거나 멈추어 서서 해돋이의 아름다움을 돌아보는 일을 기억하려면 노력이 필요합니다. 그리고 이 땅의 아름다움 뒤에 계신 창조주를 기억하는 데에는 한 걸음이 더 필요합니다. 그렇다면 우리의 일상생활이 늘 똑같다는 느낌에 얼마나 더 쉽게 빠져들어, 만나는 모든 영혼이 언젠가 하나님 앞에 설 것이라는 사실을 잊게 되겠습니까? 하나님께서 우리에게, 그분을 위해 사는 삶으로 그분을 알지 못하는 이에게 살아 계시고 참되신 한 분 하나님을 알리는 말을 하기를 바라신다면, 우리가 그 사람이 될 수도 있지 않겠습니까?

이제 가까운 곳의 일입니다…

여기에는 여러 가지 상황이 해당될 수 있습니다. 가족일 수도 있습니다. 이웃일 수도 있습니다. 조금 먼 친척일 수도 있습니다. 직장 동료일 수도 있습니다. 끝으로, 우리의 일상에서 교류하는 누구나 해당될 수 있습니다.

그때에 왕이 오른편에 있는 자들에게 이르시되 내 아버지께 복 받은 자들아, 와서 세상의 기초를 놓을 때부터 너희를 위하여 예비된 왕국을 상속하라. 내가 주릴 때에 너희가 먹을 것을 주었고, 목마를 때에 마실 것을 주었으며, 나그네 되었을 때에 영접하였고, 헐벗었을 때에 옷을 입혔으며, 병들었을 때에 찾아왔고, 감옥에 갇혔을 때에 내게 왔느니라. 그때에 의인들이 대답하여 이르되 주여, 우리가 어느 때에 주께서 주리신 것을 보고 잡수실 것을 드렸으며, 목마르신 것을 보고 마실 것을 드렸나이까? 어느 때에 주께서 나그네 되신 것을 보고 영접하였으며, 헐벗으신 것을 보고 옷을 입혔나이까? 어느 때에 주께서 병드신 것이나 감옥에 갇히신 것을 보고 주께 갔나이까? 왕이 대답하여 이르시되 진실로 내가 너희에게 이르노니 너희가 여기 내 형제 중 지극히 작은 자 하나에게 한 것이 곧 내게 한 것이니라 –마태복음 25:34-40.

제가 특히 주목하고 싶은 한 가지는 평범한 공동체들 안에서 점점 더 문제가 되고 있는 관계의 단절과 정서적·정신적 어려움입니다. 누구를 판단하려는 것도 아니고, 누구라도 기분 나쁘게 하려는 것도 아닙니다. 사실, 이러한 문제와 관련해 제가 가장 크게 염려하는 것 가운데 하나는 교회가 이러한 어려움에 따라붙는 낙인이나 부정적인 인식을 없애기 위해 할 수 있는 모든 일을 하는 것입니다. 그리스도께서는 이런 상황에 놓인 사람들과 어떻게 관계를 맺으셨습니까? 예수님께서 어떻게 응답하셨는지 세세한 부분에만 매달릴 수도 있습니다. 세세한 부분 때문에 우리 가운데 어려움을 겪는 이들에게 “그리스도처럼 행하는 것”이 방해받게 하지 맙시다.

어려움을 겪는 사람에게 어떻게 다가가고 대해야 할지 균형 있게 생각하려면, 도움이 될 몇 가지 질문을 스스로에게 해볼 수 있습니다. 먼저 자신에게 묻습니다. “내가 바로 그런 상황에 처해 있다면, 누군가가 내게 어떻게 응답해 주기를 바랄까?” 다음으로 상대방에게 묻습니다. “당신이 이 어려운 일을 겪는 동안 내가 무엇을 하면 도움이 되거나 격려가 될까요?”

너무나 자주 교회는 자기들 가운데 어려움을 겪는 이들을 돌볼 시간이 없습니다. 그들의 처지는 어쩔 수 없는 것이고, 우리는 신경 쓰기에는 너무 바쁘다고 여기기 때문입니다. 또 어떤 때는 교회가 어떻게 응답해야 할지, 무슨 말을 해야 할지 몰라서 ‘잠자는 개를 깨우지 않는 편이 낫다’거나 ‘판도라의 상자를 열지 않는 것이 낫다’고 결정합니다.

하나님께서는 우리가 형제자매들을 필요로 하도록 우리를 지으셨습니다. 성경에 나오는 서로를 대하라는 말씀들을 모두 생각해 보십시오. 그런 다음 우리 가운데 어려움을 겪는 이들에게 어떻게 “그리스도처럼 행할” 수 있을지 생각해 보십시오. 말하자면 언젠가는 ‘신발이 다른 발에 신겨질’ 때가 올 수도 있다는 점을 기억하십시오. 다시 말해, 언젠가 우리도 비슷한 상황에 놓여 형제자매들이 실제로 도움이 되는 사랑과 격려로 우리를 둘러싸 주기를 바랄 수 있습니다.

자료

하나님을 기쁘시게 하는 실천적인 길을 찾는 교회와 개인을 돕기 위해 여러 주제에 관한 엄선된 자료를 제공하고 있다는 사실을 독자 여러분께 다시 알려드린 지 한동안 되었습니다. 우리 가운데 어려움을 겪는 사람들을 어떻게 도울지 구체적으로 다루는 자료 하나는 저희가 제작한 “지역 교회에서 사람들을 돕기”라는 제목의 CD 8장 세트입니다. 여러 개인과 교회 지도자들로부터 이 세트에 담긴 정보가 자신들 가운데 있는 어려운 상황을 어떻게 “도울” 수 있을지 이해하는 데 매우 유익했다고 전해 들었습니다.

미국 내 주소로는 저희 자료를 무료로 보내드립니다. 그러나 저희 사역은 전적으로 하나님의 백성이 자원하여 드리는 헌금으로 운영되므로, 저희 사역을 계속하는 데 여러분의 후원이 도움이 됩니다. 이 CD 세트 중 하나 이상을 받고 싶으시면, 이 잡지 앞표지 안쪽에 기재된 연락처로 저희 사역 단체에 연락해 주십시오.

이제 너희를 넘어지지 아니하게 지키시고, 자신의 영광 앞에 흠 없이 큰 기쁨으로 서게 하실 수 있는 분, 곧 홀로 지혜로우신 우리 구주 하나님께 지금과 영원토록 영광과 위엄과 통치와 권능이 있기를 원하노라. 아멘. –유다서 1:24-25.

Pride is something that everyone must deal with. It is something that naturally tends to come into our lives and stay. Like many other things, it is very deceitful, because it is commonly accepted by the world in which we live. People today are proud of being proud. Americans are proud of their country, their jobs, their children, their lawns, their sports teams, their vehicles, their ambitions, their goals, their looks, their friends, their homes, and the list could go on. If we think about it, the carnal man is proud of just about anything. People stand and proclaim they are proud and boast of their great accomplishments. People look at something someone has done and proclaim to the doer, “You should be proud of yourself!”

There is one problem; God hates pride! God actually despises the proud. In Psalms, it says that God will cut off …the tongue that speaketh proud things –Psalm 12:3. And in Job it says He will …behold every one that is proud, and abase [put down or make low] him –Job 40:11. Psalms 40:4 says He will not respect the proud and in Psalm 119: Thou hast rebuked the proud that are cursed, which do err from thy commandments –Psalm 119:21. In Proverbs, we read that: The LORD will destroy the house of the proud… –Proverbs 15:25, and that Every one that is proud in heart is an abomination to the LORD… –Proverbs 16:5. In Malachi, it says that …behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud… –Malachi 4:1. Finally, James states that …God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble –James 4:6.

As we can see, the Bible is very clear on pride, and the people who are proud. There is no room for pride in our hearts or lives. So, what do we do with this? Are we proud? Do we boast as the world does?

I would like to call attention to a hidden form of pride that can slip into our lives, sometimes unnoticed. We will call it false humility. If we have a false humility, would it not actually be a form of pride?

Let us look first at Law and Grace. Someone that is under the law does not desire to do what he must do, but rather, he does it because of the law. For example, the law states that we should not kill, yet (according to the law) we are allowed to be angry. Someone can hate another and even desire to kill him, but if they resist the temptation to kill, they have indeed kept the law. Many people today who claim to be Christians, are actually under the law. They do all that they do because of a law, or an order from their authority. We can see this clearly when people push the law, doing the least that is required, but still technically keeping the law.

The head covering is a good example. A woman who desires to cover her head because of what the Bible teaches, will indeed cover her head. She does not need to be reminded to do it or be admonished for doing it half-heartedly. On the other hand, there are Christians that cover their heads; however, the actual covering continues to get smaller, and less noticeable. Some even put it all the way on the back of the head and color it the same as their hair, trying to keep it from being noticed by the uncovered public. This clearly reveals the heart; they are simply complying with the law.

This type of thinking can go for many things. One more would be adornment. The bible says that the adornment should not be outward. Many Christians will not adorn themselves with flashy eye-catching things, however there are no standards about adorning homes, vehicles, and such like. So, a plain, unadorned person gets out of their adorned vehicle and walks into their very adorned home. This shows where the heart is—under the law.

Now let us look at grace. It is the power of God in the life of a human being. It causes one to actually love their enemies, to do good to those who mistreat them. It causes one to love their God with all their heart and obey God’s commands because of a passionate love for Him. The law is no longer needed because the heart is new; it desires to live for God. When someone does evil to you, you do not think about getting even. In fact, you do not even get angry. You are a new creature and because of this power—grace from God—you love him that has done you wrong. Forgiving is not a problem; helping others is natural. You are not your own and you desire to be all you can be for your Savior who died for you.

What does this have to do with pride or humility?

The Bible says that …the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ –John 1:17. It does not take God’s Spirit in our lives for us to obey the law—we can do that on our own. Therefore, we can become proud by doing things for God because WE did them. When we did not allow our anger to spew out when disagreeing with a neighbor, we think well of ourselves, and we can become proud. However, when we actually love our neighbor that has a problem with us, we cannot become proud because it was grace; it was the power of God that caused this, not ourselves. Therefore, we marvel at God and his abundant grace.

It would be foolish for someone to be proud of something that God clearly did! If Lazarus walked around boasting of himself for being raised from the dead, people would question his sanity, saying, “You did nothing! It was Jesus that did everything.”

I’m not trying to say that the Christian does nothing. No, we must humbly obey the commandments of God and walk in His ways. However, I am saying that we cannot boast in ourselves because it is God that enables us to obey His commandments.

Let us look at the popular story of David and Goliath. David went to the army to take provisions to his brothers who were fighting there. As he approached, he marveled at what he saw, a large man challenging his people! David seemed a bit shocked, and aggrieved as he asked, …who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God? –1 Samuel 17:26.

What does David’s oldest brother Eliab say to him? “I know thy pride.”

Eliab thought the attitude of David was prideful, and we can see why. A ruddy youth walks up from tending sheep and wonders why someone is not taking care of this large man. It sounds a bit off. But what was David thinking? He was only thinking about what God could, and most likely, wanted to do! He did not think for a moment that he himself could do anything in this situation.

He is then brought before King Saul: And Saul said to David, Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou art but a youth, and he a man of war from his youth –1 Samuel 17:33.

David responded, … Thy servant kept his father’s sheep, and there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock: And I went out after him, and smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth: and when he arose against me, I caught him by his beard, and smote him, and slew him. Thy servant slew both the lion and the bear: and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them, seeing he hath defied the armies of the living God –1 Samuel 17:34-36.

David here is super confident, but why?! David said moreover, The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine… –1 Samuel 17:37.

Clearly his confidence is because the Lord is fighting for him. David was not concerned that he was “but a youth” and he did not understand why people questioned him. He was only thinking about what God was going to do! However, Eliab saw David’s confidence as pride. Possibly God had not worked in Eliab’s life. Maybe he did not know of the power of God; therefore, to him it looked like foolish pride.

And Saul armed David with his armour, and he put an helmet of brass upon his head; also he armed him with a coat of mail. And David girded his sword upon his armour, and he assayed to go; for he had not proved it. And David said unto Saul, I cannot go with these; for I have not proved them. And David put them off him –1 Samuel 17:38-39.

So, David chose to not wear the armor; it would only have been a hindrance. Rather, he chose some stones then he ran out to fight the giant. Of course, the giant also did not understand. When he …saw David, he disdained him: for he was but a youth … And the Philistine said unto David, Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods. And the Philistine said to David, Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field –1 Samuel 17:42-44.

Then David said …Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied. This day will the LORD deliver thee into mine hand; and I will smite thee … that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel –1 Samuel 17:45-46.

Notice then what David did. He killed the giant, cut off his head, and took his head back to Jerusalem. What do you think Eliab thought now? Here is the younger brother marching around the streets of Jerusalem with the head of the defeated giant! King Saul calls for David and he goes to see Saul, still holding the severed head.

Why was David not proud? Because he knew it was not he himself that did it. It was God who had done a marvelous work! He was simply testifying of the grace of God.

When we do a work on our own, we cannot boast of it because we did it. It would be pride, so we remain silent and call it humility, even if we desire others to see it. However, when it is a super-natural work of God, we now must boast of what God has done! We are called to this.

Is God working in your life? Are you confused as to whether it is you or God? Ask yourself a question, “Am I doing things that people who are not relying on God can still do?” If we are not doing anything differently than the world, then God is not working in our life. It is that simple. No one enjoys getting angry. I spent most of my childhood and teenage years going to anger management classes where counselors tried to teach us how to control our anger. The unregenerate heart can learn to hide anger, but only God can change the heart. I never heard a counselor teach us how to love people instead of getting angry with them, since it is impossible! It is only a work of the living God in one’s life, and in that work, we must boast! We testify of the outpouring of the grace of God in our lives. When someone believes it is pride, just like Eliab did, it’s because they only see the working of the Law, where all is done by man’s feeble attempts.

Let us look at an example to help us understand. If you decide to build a house, every day you put on your nail bag and get to work. It takes you time and energy, but finally the house is finished. You are standing in front of the newly constructed home with a friend. “Wow,” he states, “This house is beautiful! It looks perfectly built!”

Your cheeks blush a little and you begin to point out the flaws that you know, “No, it’s not perfect, you see that over there? I messed up on that gable…. And the siding over there… it’s not exactly straight.” We do this because we want to be humble! If we would say, “Yes, it is a beautiful house; I did a great job building it!” it would be prideful, right?

Now, what if you wanted to build a house and you realize you are not able to build it; you need God’s help. You pray for help then bam, the house is built! You never even put on your nail bag; the house miraculously appeared. God built it. Now how would the conversation go with your friend? Would you still point out all the flaws? NO! You would boast of its perfection, boldly proclaiming what the Lord had done.

When God does a work in our lives, it is not pride to tell people about it. It takes humility to say that we did not do it, but that God did! However, the devil wants us to quiet down and say it is humility like Eliab wanted David to do. We need men and women today that can boldly proclaim what God is doing in their lives!

Instead, it seems we have many defeated people that actually believe it is godly to talk down about ourselves, to act as if we are a defeated sinner trying to struggle through this earthly existence. “Rise up, Oh man of God! Be done with lesser things!”

I realize one could ask, “So, we should go around boasting about how righteous we are?” To this question, I will paint another picture. A poor criminal who has only known the city streets as home, steals and robs just to get by. He knows he is a bad person, yet he knows nothing else. One day God reveals himself to this man. In a dark alley he repents of his sin and gives his life to the Lord. God saves him, transforms him, converts him. He leaves that alley a new person! He has joy in his heart and peace in his soul!

What do you expect him to tell his friends? Um, the siding over there is not straight, the windows are too small….

NO, certainly not! Rather, he would say I’m perfect! God has done a great work, look at me! I’ve been saved by the power of God! By the blood of Jesus! All this as he skips down the road in the beauty of holiness.

Stolthet er noe alle må forholde seg til. Det er noe som naturlig har en tendens til å komme inn i livet vårt og bli værende. Som mange andre ting er den svært bedragersk, fordi den er allment akseptert i den verdenen vi lever i. Folk i dag er stolte av å være stolte. Amerikanere er stolte av landet sitt, jobbene sine, barna sine, plenene sine, idrettslagene sine, kjøretøyene sine, ambisjonene sine, målene sine, utseendet sitt, vennene sine, hjemmene sine, og listen kunne fortsette. Hvis vi tenker over det, er det kjødelige mennesket stolt av omtrent hva som helst. Folk reiser seg og erklærer at de er stolte, og skryter av sine store prestasjoner. Folk ser på noe noen har gjort og sier til den som gjorde det: «Du burde være stolt av deg selv!»

Det er ett problem: Gud hater stolthet! Gud avskyr faktisk de stolte. I Salmene står det at Gud skal la …tungen som taler store ord, bli utryddet –Salme 12:4. Og i Jobs bok står det at han skal …se på enhver som er stolt, og ydmyke [trykke ned eller gjøre lav] ham –Job 40:11. Salme 40:5 sier at han ikke har behag i de stolte, og i Salme 119 står det: Du har refset de stolte, de forbannede, som farer vill fra dine bud –Salme 119:21. I Ordspråkene leser vi: Herren river ned de stoltes hus … –Ordspråkene 15:25, og at Enhver som er stolt av hjertet, er en styggedom for Herren … –Ordspråkene 16:5. I Malaki står det at …se, dagen kommer, den brenner som en ovn, og alle de stolte … –Malaki 4:1. Til slutt sier Jakob at …Gud står de stolte imot, men de ydmyke gir han nåde –Jakob 4:6.

Som vi kan se, er Bibelen svært tydelig når det gjelder stolthet og stolte mennesker. Det er ikke rom for stolthet i hjertene eller livene våre. Så hva gjør vi med dette? Er vi stolte? Skryter vi slik verden gjør?

Jeg vil rette oppmerksomheten mot en skjult form for stolthet som kan snike seg inn i livet vårt, noen ganger uten at vi merker det. Vi kan kalle den falsk ydmykhet. Hvis vi har en falsk ydmykhet, er ikke det egentlig en form for stolthet?

La oss først se på loven og nåden. En som er under loven, ønsker ikke å gjøre det han må gjøre, men gjør det i stedet på grunn av loven. For eksempel sier loven at vi ikke skal drepe, men (ifølge loven) har vi lov til å være sinte. En kan hate en annen og til og med ønske å drepe ham, men hvis han motstår fristelsen til å drepe, har han faktisk holdt loven. Mange mennesker i dag som hevder å være kristne, er egentlig under loven. De gjør alt de gjør på grunn av en lov eller en ordre fra en autoritet. Dette ser vi tydelig når folk tøyer loven og gjør minst mulig, men likevel teknisk sett holder loven.

Hodeplagget er et godt eksempel. En kvinne som ønsker å dekke hodet på grunn av det Bibelen lærer, vil faktisk dekke hodet. Hun trenger ikke å bli minnet på det eller irettesatt fordi hun gjør det halvhjertet. På den annen side finnes det kristne som dekker hodet, men selve hodeplagget blir stadig mindre og mindre synlig. Noen plasserer det helt bak på hodet og farger det i samme farge som håret, i et forsøk på å unngå at det blir lagt merke til av folk uten hodeplagg. Dette avslører tydelig hjertet: De retter seg ganske enkelt etter loven.

Denne måten å tenke på kan gjelde mange ting. Et annet eksempel er pynt. Bibelen sier at pynten ikke skal være utvendig. Mange kristne pynter seg ikke med prangende, iøynefallende ting, men det finnes ingen regler for pynting av hjem, kjøretøy og slikt. Dermed går en enkel, upyntet person ut av sitt pyntede kjøretøy og inn i sitt svært pyntede hjem. Dette viser hvor hjertet er – under loven.

La oss nå se på nåden. Den er Guds kraft i et menneskes liv. Den får en til virkelig å elske fiendene sine og gjøre godt mot dem som behandler en dårlig. Den får en til å elske sin Gud av hele sitt hjerte og adlyde Guds bud på grunn av en brennende kjærlighet til ham. Loven trengs ikke lenger, fordi hjertet er nytt; det ønsker å leve for Gud. Når noen gjør noe ondt mot deg, tenker du ikke på å ta igjen. Faktisk blir du ikke engang sint. Du er en ny skapning, og på grunn av denne kraften – nåden fra Gud – elsker du den som har gjort deg urett. Det er ikke vanskelig å tilgi; det faller naturlig å hjelpe andre. Du tilhører ikke deg selv, og du ønsker å være alt du kan være for din Frelser, som døde for deg.

Hva har dette med stolthet eller ydmykhet å gjøre?

Bibelen sier at …loven ble gitt ved Moses, nåden og sannheten kom ved Jesus Kristus –Johannes 1:17. Vi trenger ikke Guds Ånd i livet vårt for å adlyde loven – det kan vi gjøre på egen hånd. Derfor kan vi bli stolte når vi gjør ting for Gud fordi VI gjorde dem. Når vi ikke lar sinnet vårt få fritt utløp mens vi er uenige med en nabo, synes vi godt om oss selv, og vi kan bli stolte. Men når vi virkelig elsker vår nabo som har et problem med oss, kan vi ikke bli stolte, for det var nåden; det var Guds kraft som førte til dette, ikke vi selv. Derfor undrer vi oss over Gud og hans rike nåde.

Det ville være tåpelig om noen var stolte av noe Gud tydelig hadde gjort! Hvis Lasarus gikk omkring og skrøt av at han var blitt reist opp fra de døde, ville folk tvile på hans forstand og si: «Du gjorde ingenting! Det var Jesus som gjorde alt.»

Jeg prøver ikke å si at den kristne ikke gjør noe. Nei, vi må ydmykt adlyde Guds bud og vandre på hans veier. Men jeg sier at vi ikke kan rose oss selv, for det er Gud som gjør oss i stand til å adlyde hans bud.

La oss se på den kjente fortellingen om David og Goliat. David dro til hæren for å bringe forsyninger til brødrene sine, som kjempet der. Da han nærmet seg, ble han forundret over det han så: en stor mann som utfordret folket hans! David virket litt sjokkert og opprørt da han spurte: …hvem er denne uomskårne filisteren, siden han håner den levende Guds hær? –1. Samuelsbok 17:26.

Hva sier Davids eldste bror Eliab til ham? «Jeg kjenner din stolthet.»

Eliab mente at Davids holdning var hovmodig, og vi kan forstå hvorfor. En rødmusset ung gutt kommer fra å passe sauene og lurer på hvorfor ingen tar seg av denne store mannen. Det høres litt merkelig ut. Men hva tenkte David? Han tenkte bare på hva Gud kunne gjøre, og mest sannsynlig ønsket å gjøre! Ikke et øyeblikk tenkte han at han selv kunne utrette noe i denne situasjonen.

Så blir han ført fram for kong Saul: Og Saul sa til David: «Du kan ikke gå mot denne filisteren og kjempe med ham, for du er bare en ungdom, og han har vært kriger fra ungdommen av –1. Samuelsbok 17:33.

David svarte: «…Din tjener passet sauene til sin far. Det kom en løve og en bjørn og tok et lam fra flokken. Da gikk jeg etter den, slo den og rev lammet ut av munnen på den. Da den reiste seg mot meg, grep jeg den i skjegget, slo den og drepte den. Din tjener har drept både løven og bjørnen. Denne uomskårne filisteren skal gå samme vei, siden han har hånet den levende Guds hær –1. Samuelsbok 17:34-36.

David er svært selvsikker her, men hvorfor?! David sa videre: «Herren, som reddet meg fra løvens og bjørnens klør, han skal også redde meg fra denne filisterens hånd … –1. Samuelsbok 17:37.

Det er tydelig at selvtilliten hans skyldes at Herren kjemper for ham. David var ikke bekymret for at han «bare var en ungdom», og han forsto ikke hvorfor folk stilte spørsmål ved ham. Han tenkte bare på hva Gud kom til å gjøre! Men Eliab så Davids selvtillit som stolthet. Kanskje Gud ikke hadde virket i Eliabs liv. Kanskje han ikke kjente Guds kraft; derfor så det for ham ut som tåpelig stolthet.

Saul kledde David i sin egen rustning. Han satte en bronsehjelm på hodet hans og tok på ham en brynje. David festet sverdet sitt utenpå rustningen og prøvde å gå, men han hadde ikke prøvd dette før. David sa til Saul: «Jeg kan ikke gå med dette, for jeg har ikke prøvd det.» Så tok David det av seg –1. Samuelsbok 17:38-39.

David valgte altså å ikke ha på seg rustningen; den ville bare vært til hinder. I stedet valgte han noen steiner, og så løp han ut for å kjempe mot kjempen. Kjempen forsto det selvfølgelig heller ikke. Da han …fikk øye på David, foraktet han ham, for han var bare en ungdom … Filisteren sa til David: «Er jeg en hund, siden du kommer mot meg med stokker?» Og filisteren forbannet David ved gudene sine. Filisteren sa til David: «Kom hit til meg, så skal jeg gi kjøttet ditt til himmelens fugler og markens dyr» –1. Samuelsbok 17:42-44.

Da sa David: «…Du kommer mot meg med sverd og spyd og kastespyd, men jeg kommer mot deg i navnet til Herren over hærskarene, Israels hærers Gud, han som du har hånet. I dag skal Herren gi deg i min hånd. Jeg skal slå deg … så hele jorden skal forstå at det finnes en Gud i Israel» –1. Samuelsbok 17:45-46.

Legg merke til hva David så gjorde. Han drepte kjempen, hogg hodet av ham og tok hodet med seg tilbake til Jerusalem. Hva tror dere Eliab tenkte nå? Her kommer den yngre broren marsjerende gjennom Jerusalems gater med hodet til den beseirede kjempen! Kong Saul sender bud etter David, og han går for å møte Saul mens han fortsatt holder det avhogde hodet.

Hvorfor var ikke David stolt? Fordi han visste at det ikke var han selv som hadde gjort det. Det var Gud som hadde gjort et underfullt verk! Han vitnet ganske enkelt om Guds nåde.

Når vi utfører et arbeid på egen hånd, kan vi ikke rose oss av det, for det var vi som gjorde det. Det ville være stolthet, så vi tier og kaller det ydmykhet, selv om vi ønsker at andre skal legge merke til det. Men når det er et overnaturlig verk av Gud, må vi nå rose oss av det Gud har gjort! Vi er kalt til dette.

Virker Gud i livet ditt? Er du usikker på om det er du eller Gud? Still deg selv spørsmålet: «Gjør jeg ting som mennesker som ikke stoler på Gud, også kan gjøre?» Hvis vi ikke gjør noe annerledes enn verden, virker ikke Gud i livet vårt. Så enkelt er det. Ingen liker å bli sint. Jeg tilbrakte det meste av barndommen og tenårene med å gå på kurs i sinnemestring, der rådgivere prøvde å lære oss å kontrollere sinnet vårt. Det ufornyede hjertet kan lære å skjule sinne, men bare Gud kan forandre hjertet. Jeg hørte aldri noen rådgiver lære oss hvordan vi skulle elske mennesker i stedet for å bli sinte på dem, for det er umulig! Det er bare et verk av den levende Gud i et menneskes liv, og det verket må vi rose oss av! Vi vitner om at Guds nåde er blitt utøst i livet vårt. Når noen tror at det er stolthet, slik Eliab gjorde, er det fordi de bare ser lovens virke, der alt gjøres ved menneskets ynkelige anstrengelser.

La oss se på et eksempel som kan hjelpe oss å forstå. Hvis du bestemmer deg for å bygge et hus, tar du på deg spikerbeltet hver dag og går i gang med arbeidet. Det tar tid og krefter, men til slutt står huset ferdig. Du står foran det nybygde huset sammen med en venn. «Wow», sier han, «dette huset er vakkert! Det ser helt perfekt ut!»

Du rødmer litt og begynner å peke på feilene du kjenner til: «Nei, det er ikke perfekt, ser du der borte? Jeg gjorde en feil på den gavlen … Og kledningen der borte … den er ikke helt rett.» Vi gjør dette fordi vi ønsker å være ydmyke! Hvis vi sa: «Ja, det er et vakkert hus; jeg gjorde en kjempejobb med å bygge det!» ville det være stolthet, ikke sant?

Men hva om du ønsket å bygge et hus og innså at du ikke klarte det; du trengte Guds hjelp. Du ber om hjelp, og så – pang – står huset der! Du tok aldri engang på deg spikerbeltet; huset dukket mirakuløst opp. Gud bygde det. Hvordan ville samtalen med vennen din gå nå? Ville du fortsatt peke på alle feilene? NEI! Du ville rose deg av hvor perfekt det var og frimodig fortelle hva Herren hadde gjort.

Når Gud gjør et verk i livet vårt, er det ikke stolthet å fortelle folk om det. Det krever ydmykhet å si at det ikke var vi som gjorde det, men Gud! Men djevelen vil at vi skal tie og si at det er ydmykhet, slik Eliab ville at David skulle gjøre. Vi trenger menn og kvinner i dag som frimodig kan fortelle hva Gud gjør i livet deres!

I stedet ser det ut til at vi har mange motløse mennesker som faktisk tror det er gudfryktig å snakke nedsettende om oss selv, å opptre som om vi er syndere som er slått ned og kjemper oss gjennom denne jordiske tilværelsen. «Reis deg, du Guds mann! Gjør deg ferdig med mindreverdige ting!»

Jeg forstår at noen kan spørre: «Så vi skal gå omkring og skryte av hvor rettferdige vi er?» Til dette spørsmålet vil jeg tegne et nytt bilde. En fattig forbryter som bare har kjent byens gater som hjem, stjeler og raner for å klare seg. Han vet at han er et dårlig menneske, men han kjenner ikke til noe annet. En dag åpenbarer Gud seg for denne mannen. I en mørk bakgate angrer han synden sin og gir livet sitt til Herren. Gud frelser ham, forvandler ham og omvender ham. Han går ut av bakgaten som et nytt menneske! Han har glede i hjertet og fred i sjelen!

Hva forventer du at han skal fortelle vennene sine? Eh, kledningen der borte er ikke rett, vinduene er for små …

NEI, slett ikke! Han ville heller si: «Jeg er fullkommen! Gud har gjort et stort verk, se på meg! Jeg er blitt frelst ved Guds kraft! Ved Jesu blod!» Alt dette mens han hopper nedover veien i hellighetens skjønnhet.

While the earth remaineth, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease –Genesis 8:22. Greetings to one and all. As I am writing this, it is the beginning of May and yet in our area it still seems as though spring has not yet quite arrived. There are glimmers of hope that summer surely will come—some of the trees are pushing their leaves and select early flowers have pushed their blossoms up to wave bravely in the cool, damp breezes. Yet, overall, the weather seems to feel much more like the month of March.

This coming week has the promise of warm, dry weather, which should make many area farmers and homeowners happy. We are anticipating a great bevy of activity as gardens and fields are tilled and seeded with this year’s crops. To those who read the Holy Scriptures and who believe the written Word of God, these normal day-to-day activities should be a reminder of God’s promises in the same way as each new sighting of a rainbow.

And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet. For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places –Matthew 24:6-7.

And there shall be … pestilences … in divers places

In February or March of 2020, COVID-19 was declared a pandemic (a disease that spreads rapidly and affects a large percentage of the population). Now, over two years later, health officials and government leaders are somewhat reticent to publicly declare that the crisis has passed.

Some parts of the world have lifted all regulations regarding COVID-19 such as Denmark and England, while others such as New Zealand are still quite rigid with their ongoing rules and guidelines. And quite recently Chinese officials again locked down certain areas of their country in their efforts to quash a recent outbreak of new infections.

Many, if not most, individuals are tired of it all, ready for it to be over, and anxious to get back to life as normal. Many have lost loved ones. Many have endured financial setbacks and economic loss. Recent data from the World Health Organization (WHO) provides the approximate deaths (both direct and indirect) from COVID-19 to be around 15 million for the first two years of the pandemic.

While recent data from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimates that the median global GDP dropped by 3.9% from 2019 to 2020, making it the worst economic downturn since the Great Depression, creating a global recession that is the deepest since the end of World War 2.

Recently, a brother mentioned to me that “the world is in a mess” and that he has heard realtors, auctioneers, and financial advisors say that the world of finance is in unprecedented waters and that no one knows where, when, or how it will all end.

However, we should not be surprised by this major worldwide struggle. The Scriptures foretell of famine and hunger, pestilence and death, plagues of all varieties, and the list goes on of things that will come upon the earth just prior to the end of time: …for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet –Matthew 24:6.

And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars

In recent years there have been numerous wars and rumors of wars. However, since February 24, 2022 when Russia launched its current full-scale invasion of Ukraine, there have been increased worries voiced by media and politicians about how this seems different. With the many sanctions enacted by the EU and the west, there have been ripple effects causing negative outcomes for many of the world’s economies, with sky-rocketing prices for many items and services being the outcome. Sure, there were high prices before this recent outbreak of war which was a result of the various supply chain problems that were caused by COVID-19 and its ripple effects. But since the sanctions were enacted against Russia the gas and oil prices have risen noticeably which in turn has caused the cost of most goods and services to follow suit.

What about all the what if ’s…? If this happens then “there will be a nuclear war.” If this happens then “it will cause World War 3 to begin.” “The Democrats are taking the U.S. to war with Russia.” These and many more comments are being made in our world today. To me it seems that when countries and individuals …trust in chariots, and some in horses: Psalm 20:7a, then their outcome will be that They are brought down and [are] fallen… –Psalm 20:8a. But if …we will remember the name of the LORD our God –Psalm 20:7b, then …we are risen, and [will] stand upright –Psalm 20:8b.

From my perspective it seems that many in the world have allowed fear to take root in their hearts during the whole COVID-19 ordeal. Now whenever some new “scary” development surfaces in this current Russia/Ukraine conflict and the many issues connected to it, again fear seems to be the prevailing motivator. This gives us a glimpse of what things will be like some day soon when: Men’s hearts [are] failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken –Luke 21:26. Because …those men which have not the seal of God in their foreheads … should be tormented five months … and shall desire to die, and death shall flee from them –Revelation 9:4-6. Also, there will come a day when …the kings of the earth, and the great men, and the rich men, and the chief captains, and the mighty men, and every bondman, and every free man, [will hide] themselves in the dens and in the rocks of the mountains; And [will say] to the mountains and rocks, Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb: For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand? –Revelation 6:15-17.

The worth of a soul

Then said Jesus unto his disciples, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me. For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it. For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul? –Matthew 16:24-26.

Recently, this verse came to my mind as I was thinking of a number of situations in our world today—both close to home and abroad.

First, that which is abroad…

I am one of those who enjoys relaxing on the porch of a house, which is located along a major highway, and watching the traffic. I also find it interesting to sit in an airport or bus terminal and observe the masses of people passing by. Many times, I have paused to consider that each one has a soul that will spend all of eternity somewhere! Alive! As I’ve pondered these thoughts, some further thoughts also come. “How many of these people have a personal awareness of eternity?” “Of life after death?” “Or of a God who is alive, sovereign, and holy who will some day require an accounting for all things done in this earthly body?”

How many of us bear a burden for the lost souls around us? I think of the testimony of a vehicle mechanic who told me how he prays and seeks the Lord’s leading about how he can speak into the lives of those who come to his shop. And of his further testimony regarding the various ways that God has led and folks have been pointed to a Living God and a life after death.

For many of us, for me in particular, it takes an effort to remember to stop and smell the roses or to pause and reflect on the beauty of a sunrise. Then it takes a further step to remember the Creator behind these earthly beauties. How much more can we become lulled into the sameness of our everyday lives and tend to forget that each soul we meet will someday stand before God? What if we were the one who God wanted to say a word for Him out of a life that was living for Him to bring His awareness to one who knows not the One, Living, and True God?

Now for that which is close…

This can take on many different situations. It can be those in our family. It can be our neighbors. It can be our more distant relatives. It can be our work associates. Finally, it can be anyone who we interact with in our daily lives.

And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me –Matthew 25:34-40.

One specific thing that I wish to focus on is this growing problem of broken relationships and emotional/mental struggles within the plain communities. I do not wish to pass judgment on anyone, nor do I wish to make anyone feel bad. In fact, one of my strongest concerns regarding these issues is that the church would do everything that it can to take away the stigma or negativity of these struggles. How did Christ relate to those who were in these types of situations? We could get hung up on the details of how Jesus responded. Let’s not allow details to hinder us from “being Christ” to these struggling individuals in our midst.

To bring perspective to how we approach and interact with someone who is struggling, we can ask ourselves several questions that will help. First a question for myself: “How would I appreciate someone responding to me if I was in that specific situation?” Second a question for the other person: “What can I do that would be a help or an encouragement to you as you are going through this difficult experience?”

Too many times, the church doesn’t have time for those who are struggling in their midst, since it is their lot in life and we are too busy to be bothered. Other times, the church doesn’t know how to respond or what to say so they decide it is better to “leave sleeping dogs lie” or that it would be best to not “open that can of worms”.

God designed us in such a way that we need our brothers and sisters. Just consider all the “one-anothering” passages in the Scriptures. Then consider how we can “be Christ” to the struggling among us. Just remember that there may come a time when “the shoe is on the other foot”, so to speak. In other words, someday we may find ourselves in a similar situation wishing that our brothers and sisters would rally around us with love and encouragement in a real way that “helps”.

Resources

It has been a while since we have reminded our readers that we have select resources on a variety of topics to assist churches and individuals as they seek a practical way forward that is pleasing to God. One resource, that is specific on the topic of how to help those in our midst, is an 8 CD set we put together titled “People Helping in the Local Church”. We have received feedback from many individuals and church leaders who have said that they found the information shared in this set to be very helpful in their efforts to understand how to “help” challenging situations in their midst.

Our resources are available free of charge to addresses located within the U.S. However, we are funded solely on the free-will offerings of God’s people, so your donation would be helpful to continue our work. Пока земля существует, сеяние и жатва, холод и жара, лето и зима, день и ночь не прекратятся — Бытие 8:22. Приветствую всех. Пишу это в начале мая, и всё же в наших краях кажется, будто весна ещё не совсем наступила. Появляются проблески надежды, что лето непременно придёт: на некоторых деревьях распускаются листья, а первые цветы смело поднимают бутоны, чтобы приветствовать прохладный влажный ветерок. И всё же в целом погода скорее напоминает март.

На следующей неделе обещают тёплую сухую погоду, что должно порадовать многих местных фермеров и домовладельцев. Мы ожидаем большого оживления: огороды и поля будут вспахивать и засевать урожаем этого года. Для тех, кто читает Священное Писание и верит написанному Слову Божьему, эти обычные повседневные дела должны служить напоминанием об обетованиях Бога, как и каждый новый увиденный нами радугой.

Также услышите о войнах и военных слухах. Смотрите, не ужасайтесь, ибо надлежит всему тому быть, но это ещё не конец. Ибо восстанет народ на народ, и царство на царство; и будут голод, моры и землетрясения по местам — Матфея 24:6-7.

И будут … моры … по местам

В феврале или марте 2020 года COVID-19 был объявлен пандемией (болезнью, которая быстро распространяется и поражает значительную часть населения). Теперь, более двух лет спустя, представители органов здравоохранения и руководители правительств не спешат публично заявлять, что кризис миновал.

В некоторых частях мира отменили все правила, касающиеся COVID-19, например в Дании и Англии, тогда как в других, например в Новой Зеландии, по-прежнему строго соблюдают действующие правила и рекомендации. А совсем недавно китайские власти вновь ввели локдаун в некоторых районах страны, пытаясь подавить новую вспышку заражений.

Многие, если не большинство людей, устали от всего этого, хотят, чтобы всё закончилось, и стремятся вернуться к обычной жизни. Многие потеряли близких. Многие понесли финансовые потери и столкнулись с экономическими трудностями. По недавним данным Всемирной организации здравоохранения (ВОЗ), за первые два года пандемии от COVID-19 умерло примерно 15 миллионов человек — как непосредственно, так и косвенно.

В то же время, согласно недавним данным Международного валютного фонда (МВФ), медианный мировой ВВП с 2019 по 2020 год сократился на 3,9%, что стало самым резким экономическим спадом со времён Великой депрессии и привело к глобальной рецессии, глубочайшей со времён окончания Второй мировой войны.

Недавно один брат сказал мне, что «мир в полном беспорядке», и рассказал, что слышал от риелторов, аукционистов и финансовых консультантов, будто мир финансов оказался в беспрецедентной ситуации и никто не знает, где, когда и как всё это закончится.

Однако эта масштабная мировая борьба не должна нас удивлять. Писание предсказывает голод и нужду, мор и смерть, всевозможные бедствия, и этот список того, что обрушится на землю незадолго до конца времён, продолжается: …надлежит всему тому быть, но это ещё не конец — Матфея 24:6.

Также услышите о войнах и военных слухах

В последние годы было много войн и слухов о войнах. Однако после того, как 24 февраля 2022 года Россия начала нынешнее полномасштабное вторжение в Украину, СМИ и политики стали чаще выражать обеспокоенность тем, что нынешняя ситуация чем-то отличается от прежних. Многочисленные санкции, введённые ЕС и странами Запада, вызвали цепную реакцию и негативно сказались на экономике многих стран мира; в результате цены на многие товары и услуги резко взлетели. Конечно, ещё до этой недавней вспышки войны цены были высокими из-за различных проблем в цепочках поставок, вызванных COVID-19 и его последствиями. Но после введения санкций против России заметно подорожали газ и нефть, что, в свою очередь, привело к росту цен на большинство товаров и услуг.

А как насчёт всех этих «а что, если…»? Если это случится, то «начнётся ядерная война». Если это случится, то «начнётся Третья мировая война». «Демократы ведут США к войне с Россией». Сегодня в мире звучит множество подобных и других заявлений. Мне кажется, что когда страны и люди …на колесницы, иные на коней — Псалом 19:8а, тогда итогом будет то, что Они поколебались и пали… — Псалом 19:9а. Но если …мы именем Господа Бога нашего хвалимся — Псалом 19:8б, тогда …мы встали и стоим прямо — Псалом 19:9б.

На мой взгляд, многие люди в мире позволили страху укорениться в их сердцах во время всего испытания, связанного с COVID-19. Теперь, когда в нынешнем конфликте между Россией и Украиной и во множестве связанных с ним проблем появляется какое-нибудь новое «пугающее» развитие событий, страх вновь, кажется, становится главной движущей силой. Это даёт нам представление о том, что будет происходить в недалёком будущем, когда: Люди будут издыхать от страха и ожидания бедствий, грядущих на вселенную, ибо силы небесные поколеблются — Луки 21:26. Потому что …те люди, которые не имеют печати Божией на челах своих … должны были мучиться пять месяцев … и будут искать смерти, но не найдут её; пожелают умереть, но смерть убежит от них — Откровение 9:4-6. Также наступит день, когда …цари земные, и вельможи, и богатые, и тысяченачальники, и сильные, и всякий раб, и всякий свободный, [спрячутся] в пещерах и ущельях гор; И [скажут] горам и камням: падите на нас и сокройте нас от лица Сидящего на престоле и от гнева Агнца; ибо пришёл великий день гнева Его, и кто может устоять? — Откровение 6:15-17.

Ценность души

Тогда Иисус сказал ученикам Своим: если кто хочет идти за Мною, отвергнись себя, и возьми крест свой, и следуй за Мною. Ибо кто хочет душу свою сберечь, тот потеряет её; а кто потеряет душу свою ради Меня, тот обретёт её. Какая польза человеку, если он приобретёт весь мир, а душе своей повредит? или какой выкуп даст человек за душу свою? — Матфея 16:24-26.

Недавно, размышляя о разных обстоятельствах в современном мире — как поблизости, так и за рубежом, — я вспомнил этот стих.

Сначала о том, что происходит вдали…

Мне нравится отдыхать на веранде дома, стоящего у оживлённого шоссе, и наблюдать за движением. Мне также интересно сидеть в аэропорту или на автобусном вокзале и смотреть на толпы проходящих мимо людей. Часто я останавливался и думал о том, что у каждого из них есть душа, которой предстоит провести вечность где-то! Живая душа! Размышляя об этом, я задавался и другими вопросами: «Многие ли из этих людей сознают, что их ждёт вечность?» «Знают ли они о жизни после смерти?» «Знают ли они о живом, владычествующем и святом Боге, Который однажды потребует отчёта за всё, сделанное в этом земном теле?»

Сколько из нас несёт бремя за погибающие души вокруг нас? Я вспоминаю свидетельство автомеханика, который рассказал мне, как молится и ищет водительства Господа, чтобы понять, как говорить о вере с людьми, приходящими к нему в мастерскую. Он также рассказывал о разных случаях, когда Бог направлял его и люди обращались к живому Богу и узнавали о жизни после смерти.

Многим из нас, и мне в особенности, приходится прилагать усилия, чтобы не забывать остановиться и вдохнуть аромат роз или задержаться и поразмышлять о красоте восхода. А затем нужно сделать ещё один шаг — вспомнить о Творце, Который стоит за этими земными красотами. Насколько легче нам погрузиться в однообразие повседневной жизни и забыть, что каждая встреченная нами душа однажды предстанет перед Богом! А что, если именно нам Бог хотел поручить сказать от Его имени слово, чтобы через жизнь, посвящённую Ему, открыть Его тому, кто не знает Единого, Живого и Истинного Бога?

Теперь о том, что рядом…

Это может касаться самых разных людей. Это могут быть члены нашей семьи. Наши соседи. Более дальние родственники. Коллеги по работе. Наконец, любой человек, с которым мы общаемся в повседневной жизни.

Тогда скажет Царь тем, которые по правую сторону Его: приидите, благословенные Отца Моего, наследуйте Царство, уготованное вам от создания мира: ибо алкал Я, и вы дали Мне есть; жаждал, и вы напоили Меня; был странником, и вы приняли Меня; был наг, и вы одели Меня; был болен, и вы посетили Меня; в темнице был, и вы пришли ко Мне. Тогда праведники скажут Ему в ответ: Господи! когда мы видели Тебя алчущим, и накормили? или жаждущим, и напоили? когда мы видели Тебя странником, и приняли? или нагим, и одели? когда мы видели Тебя больным, или в темнице, и пришли к Тебе? И Царь скажет им в ответ: истинно говорю вам: так как вы сделали это одному из сих братьев Моих меньших, то сделали Мне — Матфея 25:34-40.

Особенно я хотел бы обратить внимание на растущую проблему разрушенных отношений и эмоциональных и душевных трудностей в общинах, придерживающихся простого уклада жизни. Я не хочу никого осуждать и не хочу, чтобы кому-либо стало неловко или стыдно. Напротив, одна из моих главных забот в связи с этими проблемами заключается в том, чтобы церковь делала всё возможное для преодоления стигмы и негативного отношения к таким трудностям. Как Христос относился к людям в подобных обстоятельствах? Мы можем увязнуть в подробностях того, как отвечал Иисус. Не будем позволять этим подробностям мешать нам быть Христом для тех, кто борется с трудностями среди нас.

Чтобы понять, как нам обращаться с человеком, переживающим трудности, и как взаимодействовать с ним, можно задать себе несколько полезных вопросов. Сначала вопрос к себе: «Как бы я хотел, чтобы кто-нибудь отнёсся ко мне, окажись я в подобной ситуации?» Затем вопрос к другому человеку: «Что я могу сделать, чтобы помочь тебе или поддержать тебя, пока ты проходишь через это трудное испытание?»

Слишком часто церкви не хватает времени на тех, кто переживает трудности среди них: мол, такова их доля, а мы слишком заняты, чтобы этим заниматься. В других случаях церковь не знает, как отреагировать и что сказать, и потому решает, что лучше «не будить лихо» или что лучше «не открывать этот ящик Пандоры».

Бог устроил нас так, что мы нуждаемся в братьях и сёстрах. Только вспомните все места Писания, в которых говорится о том, что мы должны делать друг для друга. Затем подумайте, как мы можем быть Христом для тех, кто борется с трудностями среди нас. Помните: может наступить время, когда, как говорится, «ботинок окажется на другой ноге». Иными словами, однажды мы сами можем оказаться в похожей ситуации и захотеть, чтобы братья и сёстры окружили нас любовью и ободрением и по-настоящему помогли.

Ресурсы

Давно мы не напоминали читателям, что у нас есть подборка материалов на самые разные темы, которые помогают церквям и отдельным людям найти практический путь вперёд, угодный Богу. Один из материалов, непосредственно посвящённый тому, как помогать тем, кто рядом с нами, — это комплект из 8 CD под названием «Помощь людям в поместной церкви». Многие люди и церковные руководители поделились с нами, что сведения из этого комплекта очень помогли им понять, как оказывать помощь в сложных ситуациях, возникающих среди них.

Наши материалы предоставляются бесплатно тем, кто живёт в США. Однако наша работа финансируется исключительно добровольными пожертвованиями Божьего народа, поэтому ваши пожертвования помогут нам продолжать наше служение. Если вы хотите получить один или несколько таких комплектов CD, свяжитесь с нашим служением, используя контактную информацию, указанную на внутренней стороне передней обложки этого журнала.

Могущему же соблюсти вас от падения и поставить пред славою Своею непорочными в радости, Единому Премудрому Богу, Спасителю нашему через Иисуса Христа Господа нашего, слава и величие, сила и власть прежде всех веков, ныне и во все веки. Аминь. — Иуды 1:24-25.
